name: Server-Timing header
plain: Servers send timing metrics to the page through a response header.
meaning: Lets a backend or CDN expose database, cache and edge timings to client JavaScript, for monitoring or for leaking server state when cross-origin readable.

data.metric: Each metric name plus dur in ms

limits.headline: Can pass timing numbers from the server to page scripts
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as the page loads
can: Send database, cache and edge time numbers in a response header
Let page code see those numbers
Show server details when another site allows other sites to see them
cannot: Show you the numbers by itself
Show another site's timings without that site's approval

story.what_it_is: A website's server sends timing numbers to the page, such as how long the database took.

marketing.name: Server-Timing header
marketing.pitch: Explains how servers can pass timing about their work to the browser for tools and analytics.

story.for_you: You never see it. When a page loads, the server may say it took 120 ms to look something up. That number goes into the browser tools and helps the team fix slow pages.
story.for_makers: Teams use it to see exactly where a page spends time, in the server, cache or database, right from real visitors. It also lets edge networks report cache hits, so teams can tune them.

use_cases.example: A retailer sees that a product page waits 400 ms on its stock database, and speeds it up.
A developer reads timing in browser tools to see if a slow page is the server or the network.
A monitoring service collects server timing from real visitors and charts slow steps.
A news site learns that its CDN missed the cache for a viral story and fixes the rules.
A game site checks how long the matchmaking call takes before a player joins a lobby.
A bank tracks how long each login step takes on the server to find slow spots.
A site sees that server time spikes during an attack and uses the numbers to respond.

risks: Seen by scripts on the page

technical_bounds: Not a fingerprint, reveals server side state

value.legit_uses: Performance debugging and CDN diagnostics (Cloudflare, Fastly, Vercel)
value.abuse: Server can tag visitors for correlation, cross-origin side channels with TAO
